exposure: Elective induction of labor at 39 weeks gestation
cohort: 10,758 low-risk nulliparous and multiparous patients delivering live, non-anomalous singletons at ≥39 weeks gestational age
finding: An institutional policy offering elective induction of labor at 39 weeks gestation to low-risk patients was associated with a lower cesarean birth rate, lower birth weights, and lower neonatal hypoglycemia, but an increased risk of chorioamnionitis and hemorrhage.
